result:
Solution 3 is wrong. Its upper bound at 1/4 is weaker than the Letzter–Snyder bound of 1/5, which gives the property for every c > 1/5 with a {C₃,C₅}-free (hence triangle-free) target. So 1/4 cannot be the infimum. Its lower-bound claim also conflicts with that result: graphs with odd girth ≥ 7 and minimum degree above n/5 map to a bounded-size graph, so they have bounded chromatic number, which contradicts the claimed large-χ construction at minimum degree about n/4.

Solutions 1 and 2 both give 1/5. I could not verify the literature citations, so this rests on recollection. The upper bound is consistent with the Letzter–Snyder result. The matching lower bound for triangle-free targets is the less certain step. Solution 1 states the lower bound in the exact setting the question asks about, with triangle-free targets, so I prefer it. Solution 2 gets there through a looser chain of citations.

CHOICE: 1
